title: Koszul tensor and tail comparisons preserve Roos projection adjoints
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $t$ a global section such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. Put $B_m=R/t^mR$ and $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, augmented to $B_m$, for $m\geq1$. Let $X_\bullet$ be a strict inverse sequence of unbounded $R$-complexes and let $H=R\!\lim_nX_n$ with its projections $p_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Countable products of $R$-modules are exact and derived products are represented termwise; write $\mathsf R(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$ for the Roos model [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For every $h\geq1$, deleting the levels $n<h$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathsf R(X)\to\mathsf R(X|_{n\geq h})$ compatible with the remaining projections. The canonical tensor/product and cone identifications give a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R\to B_m}(H\otimes_R^LB_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\!\lim_{n\geq h}(X_n\otimes_RK_m)$$
in $D(R)$, where $K_m$ computes the restricted derived tensor. Under it, the projection to $X_n\otimes_RK_m$ is the derived tensor of $p_n$, with the canonical two-term comparison.

More precisely, fix $h=m$, a complex $N$ of $B_m$-modules and a strict compatible family of $B_m$-linear chain maps $f_n:X_n\otimes_RB_m\to N$ for $n\geq m$. Compose the last isomorphism with the derived limit of the augmentations $X_n\otimes_RK_m\to X_n\otimes_RB_m$, then with $R\!\lim f_n$ and the diagonal identification $R\!\lim\operatorname{const}(N)\cong N$. The resulting morphism is the restriction of the adjoint, under the derived tensor--restriction adjunction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], of $H\xrightarrow{p_m}X_m\to\operatorname{Res}N$, the second map being $x\mapsto f_m(x\otimes1)$. Restriction to $D(R)$ detects isomorphisms in $D(B_m)$. These identifications commute with the coefficient quotient transitions: for $k\leq m$ the Koszul transition $K_m\to K_k$ is $(t^{m-k},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$. Finally, if all $X_n$ have cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$, then $H$ has cohomology in $[a,b+1]$, without a quasi-compactness hypothesis on $T$.

The explicitly defined comparison is invertible because its factors are isomorphisms and deletion is a quasi-isomorphism. Expanding its composite proves naturality; checking the current Roos coordinate on each total-tensor summand gives the projection identity.

proof.text: For a constant complex N define the finite-prefix-sum map v on its product by v(z)_0=0 and v(z)_(n+1)=v(z)_n-z_n. Then vu=1 and uv=1-pr_0 diagonal. The Roos triangle and this splitting show that evaluation at zero and the strict Roos lift of the diagonal are mutually inverse after localization, with the stated coordinates.

proof.text: For a K-flat complex the augmentation-adjoint identity is exactly the derived-adjunction and A_kflat normalizations. For an arbitrary complex precompose with a K-flat resolution; naturality of A and the augmentation and the ordinary and derived Hom equivalences cancel this invertible replacement. Expand the strict family map and use the projection identity to prove the required full derived adjoint equation.

proof.text: Exact countable products commute with homology, so the product of the strict tower complexes has vanishing cohomology outside [a,b]. Apply the homology exact sequence to the actual Roos mapping-cocone triangle: H^(q-1)(product) and H^q(product) vanish for q outside [a,b+1]. Transport this vanishing through norm. Assemble these properties with the normalization into Compatibility and hence Conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRoosProjectionComparison (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t})
    [EssentiallySmall.{t + 1} T.ProEt]
    (R : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{max z (t + 1)})
    (s : (R.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{max z (t + 1)}).sections)
    [∀ S : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{max z (t + 1)},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules S)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Modules R)]
    (_hs : Mono (globalSectionMultiplication R (unitSection R s))) :
    Conclusion R s
lean.note: All maps use the existing principal-power quotient sheaves, principal Koszul complexes, total sheaf tensor and strict Roos functor. Models stores comparison data; Normalization and Compatibility give its universal properties and all canonical-map equations. Conclusion includes existence of ring sheafification, available on the essentially small site, without a mathematical sheafification hypothesis. Positive indices are represented by predecessors and tensor is in the canonically symmetric scalar-first convention.
